_README: THE CONTRACT FILE. Only literals that cross a HALF BOUNDARY live here --
a string or pattern that the CLI, the agent and/or the web UI must agree on
to the character. Read by all three: ConvertFrom-Json via Scripts/Get-Consts.ps1,
json.load via agent/core/consts.py, a build-time import via web/src/shell/consts.ts.
WHAT DOES NOT GO HERE. A literal only one half ever types (a help sentence, a
UI label, a log message, an anchor the CLI both writes and reads) stays in that
half's own constants -- AGENTS.md, 'One place for magic strings'. Nor is this a
second source of truth beside config.default.json, which keeps workItemTypes,
commands and orgs: those are CONFIGURATION, which a team may change. These are
the CONTRACT, which nobody may change alone.
Templates keep their literal text. They are documents a person reads, not parsers.
REGEXES TRAVEL AS STRINGS and each half compiles its own, in the subset .NET,
Python and JS agree on. A pattern that cannot be written that way stays in code
THE VERSION is the product's, one string for all three halves. The module
manifest (Prompt20Toolkit/Prompt20Toolkit.psd1, written by its generator from
this key) and web/package.json carry their own literal; the three suites fail
naming the file when one of them does not say the same.

repository._: The package's own repository, as an address. What the agent compares a Space's repository with when the package has no git origin to read -- a copy installed without .git -- so the Space that is this package itself still reads as itself (the Prompts card's isToolkit, docs/modules/studio.md). A checkout's origin wins when it is there, so a fork that makes itself a Space reads as the fork. The public export's repo-name rule renames it in the public tree.

stamps._: Written by Scripts/Write-CardText.ps1's callers; read by the engagement summary's billed days and the web's session cards. assigned is who takes a card with no issue behind it -- `**Assigned:** me`, or a size (a worker label) -- written by Route -Assign and read by the card model's `assigned` (docs/hub/cards.md).

tokens._: Lines in a card whose exact text is a state gate or a section anchor more than one half looks for. design and spec name the design a card was worked against (design.cardLineRegex reads them).

regex._: The state machine, which exists once per half on purpose and must not drift. Get-PromptStatus.ps1 and agent/core/parsers.py were the two copies. commitBullet captures the hash in group 1, so the lane rule and the standup's commit count read the bullet through one pattern (a findall with one group returns the hashes, and their number is the count). -- cardId: The shape of a card's id, WITHOUT anchors -- each reader composes '^(prefix)?(<cardId>)-' around it. Two shapes: a work item number (all digits), or a card with no work item: four characters from an alphabet with no look-alikes (no 0 O 1 I L B 8 S 5 Z), at least one digit AND at least one letter -- so it can never read as a work item number, and never as a type prefix (TASK, FEAT). Uppercase, and matched case-SENSITIVELY, so a lowercase slug can never read as an id. The two lookaheads are the subset .NET, Python and JS share.

status._: The derived state of a card. There is no status field anywhere -- these strings ARE the vocabulary, and the web sorts and colours by them. backlog and done are FOLDER states, read first and whatever the card's text says: a card in backlog/ is Backlog (planned, not in play), a card in archive/ is Done. Tests/fixtures/parsers/states.json holds both halves' readers to one table (docs/hub/cards.md, "State is derived, never stored").

folders._: The folders a card lives in, under an org's promptsFolder: current/ (in play), archive/ (done) and backlog/ (planned, not yet in play -- where NewPrompt writes unless told -Now; a Space's folder only, a hub-root sibling such as growth/ or manager/ has none). Under each hub-root sibling, current/ and archive/. And assets, the Space's sibling of the three, where a card keeps what is not text: assets/<card key>/cover.png (docs/hub/cards.md, "A card's pictures").

assets._: A card's pictures (docs/hub/cards.md, "A card's pictures"). coverExtensions are the image types Cover accepts, lowercase, no dot; the agent's GET /api/assets route serves exactly these, and the model's cover and before are null for any other. coverMaxBytes is the largest image Cover copies (5 MB): the hub may be a repository that syncs, and a cover is a screen snap, not a recording. Cover refuses over it and names the number. Tests/fixtures/parsers/covers.json holds the CLI's and the agent's readers of the **Cover:** / **Before:** line to one table.

features._: Which keys of a Space's features block are the SPACE's rather than the engineer's. Every other flag lives in the top-level features block and holds steady across activeSpace; these are read from spaces[].features, and a Space cannot set anything else. A key here is a boolean flag (sprintAwareness; suggestions, the suggestion rule's off switch -- unset is on wherever Team Agile is on, false turns the chair's Next line back to briefNextNone) or a number a Space states (trainingHoursPerQuarter, whole hours; absent means no requirement): the merged features map /env serves carries the flags only, and a number is read off the Space itself. utilities.psm1 (SpaceScopedFeatures), agent/core/config.py (SPACE_FEATURES) and web/src/shell/consts.ts (FEATURES.spaceScoped) all read this list; tkEnv and the System page's EnvCard render the result.

reviews._: reviews/<slug-set>/<year>/<start>_<end>/<fileName>. Generate-Review.ps1 writes the tree; agent/ado/reporting.py reads it.

reminders._: The Organize add-on's reminders. buckets are the three derived readings, in display order -- computed at read time against the local clock by the CLI's Reminders and the agent's GET /api/reminders, never stored (Tests/fixtures/reminders/buckets.json holds the two to one table); the web filters by them. snooze is what -Snooze takes and what the card's menu offers.

env._: Environment variables one half SETS and another READS. teamsWebhookPrefix is the front of every TEAMS_WEBHOOK_<RECIPIENT> variable (gate 2 of a send) -- the engine, the CLI script and the three test runners agree on it, so a runner can clear every webhook by pattern. testRunMarker is set by every test runner and read by the two things that can post to a real webhook: while it is set, nothing posts. agentPort carries web.agentPort (the config key, resolved by Scripts/Get-AgentPort.ps1) from the launcher to the two proxies that cannot read config: Start-Web.ps1 sets it, web/vite.config.ts reads it for the dev proxy, and docker-compose.yml passes it to nginx's envsubst template. The name itself is what has to agree; the value is configuration. activeSpace and features are the two per-PROCESS stand-ins for config.local.json that `Web -Dev -Fixture` sets for the servers it starts, so a smoke run never rewrites the machine's config: activeSpace is a Space slug and replaces config.local.json's activeSpace; features is a JSON object and replaces config.local.json's top-level features block ({} = no flag set). Read by utilities.psm1 through Scripts/Resolve-HubConfig.ps1 and by agent/core/config.py's load_config. agentCacheDir moves the agent's on-disk cache (agent/core/disk_cache.py: the Design tab's parsed rows and note bodies, by blob sha) off the platform's user cache folder: the two test runners point it at a scratch folder so no suite writes the real one.

agent._: Where the agent listens. bindHost is the one interface Scripts/Start-Agent.ps1 hands uvicorn as --host: the loopback, so the agent answers the machine it runs on and nothing else. The agent has no authentication of its own, so this literal IS the boundary; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, Trust model. Tests/test_consts.py (TheAgentListensOnTheLoopbackOnly) holds the script, the compose file and the settings to it, and the three consts suites state the value.

tests._: The three halves a test run covers, in the order {cliPrefix}Test runs them. test-summary.<machine>.json tags every suite entry with one of them (`half`) and holds one record per half under `halves`; the CLI runner and Test write it (Scripts/TestAll-Rules.ps1), agent/core/log.py serves it on GET /api/test-history, and the System page's Health card and Setup draw it in this order. legacyHalf is what an entry with no `half` is read as: the file was the CLI runner's alone before the halves existed.

spaces._: A shipped Space's slug that changed, old -> new (the Azure demo was once 'test'). Read by both loaders so a machine whose hub.json or config.local.json still names the old slug keeps its Space. One rule: an old slug means its new Space while no Space is declared under the old one and one is under the new. A hub.json entry under an old slug that carries no 'name' is judged against the shipped slugs -- it is a patch on the shipped Space, read under the new slug with its promptsFolder kept (one that names itself is a Space of its own -- which is how Tests/fixtures/hub keeps its 'test'); a config.local.json patch, an activeSpace or a slug a person types, under an old slug, means the new Space whenever no Space is declared under the old one. Scripts/Resolve-HubConfig.ps1 (Get-P20RenamedSpaceSlugs, Resolve-P20RenamedSlug) and agent/core/config.py (renamed_slug) read it, and Tests/fixtures/space-renamed/table.json is the one table both suites assert. The web never reads it -- it reads /api/env -- but the contract is stated on all three sides.

visibility._: Whether a GitHub Space's repository is public: the three words a Space's visibility is served and printed as, lowercase. The agent reads it once per repository (gh api repos/{owner}/{repo} -> visibility) and serves it on GET /api/visibility; the CLI reads it the same way for Env, SwitchSpace Status and its writing verbs; the web draws it on the Spaces card's GitHub rows, beside the active Space's name and over a write. gh's INTERNAL (an enterprise repository, not read by strangers) is served as private. A Space spanning several repositories is public when any of them is, private when all of them are, unknown otherwise. unknown is what a tracker that did not answer gives -- never a guess, and drawn as unknown. An Azure DevOps Space, or one with no tracker, has no visibility at all: the rule is not asked there. publicLine is the one line a write to a public repository carries, in the web's write dialogs and before a CLI verb writes (-WhatIf included).

docs._: The Docs tab of a GitHub Space (D-S12): which of a repo's files are the product's documentation. readme is the landing page at the repo root; root is the folder whose markdown tree sits beside it; segment is what one path segment may look like (so '..', '.', an empty segment, a backslash or a space never is one). The agent's /api/docs routes refuse any path that is neither (and anything with '..' in it); the web's link resolver opens exactly those paths in the reading room and sends every other relative link to github.com -- one rule, so the two cannot disagree about what is a doc. landingUrl is a different thing with a similar name: the PUBLIC marketing page (web/landing.html, built by `npm run build:landing`), deployed to GitHub Pages on every push to main -- not a Docs-tab file at all. The README's Documentation table links it as a literal, and this is the one address the app's Home foot reads so the two never drift apart.

studio._: The Studio's design notes (docs/modules/studio.md, "The file shape, and how a note is read"). noteName is what one note's file name may be -- one markdown file, no path: NewDesign writes only names that match it, the agent's /api/studio/design/{name} refuses any other, and the web opens exactly those in the reading room. threadLine is the line that names a document's thread, `> GitHub: <issue url>` -- the same line a card and an issue file carry; the CLI writes it (Promote, through Write-CardText) and threadRegex is how the agent reads it back, from a hub note and from a repo's design/ and spec/ alike: group 1 the URL, 2 the owner, 3 the repo, 4 the number. promoteLabel is the label Promote (NewItem -FromDesign) puts on the issue it opens, and the web's Promote dialog names it -- review happens in the tracker's thread (D-S5). promptsRoute is the Studio's Prompts card's read: the agent mounts it, the web asks it -- the list of agentic/'s shipped prompts and your hub's, and one prompt's text below it.

design._: The design lifecycle's identity (L1; docs/hub/design.md, "The file"). A design carries an id in its file's frontmatter under idKey; a spec carries the SAME id as the note it graduated from. idRegex is the shape of that id -- a UUID v4, lowercase, hyphenated, anchored -- which NewDesign and StampDesign write, the agent will read and the web will show. states are the four names a design's state can have (derived from where its files are, never stored) and outcomes the two a note archived without a spec may carry as `**Outcome:**`. L2 (the reader) derives the state in the agent and the CLI by one rule, Tests/fixtures/design/states.json; outcome is read from the note's `**Outcome:**` line (stamps.outcome), which MoveDesign (L3) writes. docsLine is the line a completed spec carries naming where its durable part landed, `> Docs: <path>` -- written by MoveDesign -To Complete, read by the agent for a Complete row; docsRegex reads it back, group 1 the path. cardLineRegex is how both halves read the line a CARD carries naming the design it was worked against (C3; docs/hub/cards.md, "2. The sections -- by type, from the template"): `> Design: [<title>](<link>) <id>`, written by NewPrompt -Design under the card's `> Template:` line (tokens.design), and the corpus's hand-written `> Spec: [<title>](<link>) <words>` (tokens.spec), read as written. Group 1 is the word (Design or Spec), 2 the link's text, 3 its target, 4 what follows -- the design's id when it is one (design.idRegex), else the person's words. A card names one design: its first Design line, else its first Spec line. Scripts/Read-DesignTree.ps1 (Get-P20CardDesign) and agent/core/parsers.py (card_design) are held to one table, Tests/fixtures/parsers/design-lines.json.

rituals._: Solitaire Agile's Ritual Engine (docs/modules/solitaire-agile.md, "The file shape, and how a standup is read"). Two halves render the SAME standup text -- the CLI's Standup and the agent's GET /api/ritual/standup, which the web shows verbatim -- so the words both type live here. triageRoute is the triage ceremony's read: the open issues by milestone, which the CLI's Triage prints and the web's Triage page asks one at a time. assignMe is the one answer to who takes an item that is not a size (D-AR10): Route -Assign me (the web's third question sends it), the value a card's **Assigned:** line carries for you, and each triage item's who when its GitHub assignee is the signed-in gh user; an item's who is otherwise @<login> for another assignee, else its size (the worker label), else empty -- nobody. ceremoniesFile and vocabularyFile are the data files under Config/ both halves read. workerLabelPrefix is how a tracker label says it routes to a worker (its description starts with it; the name after it up to the ' -- ' separator is the worker's). labelWidth is the column the slot labels are padded to. text holds every fixed string of the rendering; Tests/fixtures/rituals/ holds the table and the golden texts both suites assert. The reminder to attend (D-TA15) is an Organize reminder: remindSource is the **Source:** tag it carries and remindTitle its title, both written by the CLI (Standup -Remind, and attending) and matched by the agent (POST attendRoute re-arms it through the bridge; GET remindRoute is what the settings row reads); weekdays are the day names a cadence is written in, Monday first, and remindDays the cadence -Days defaults to. The cadence itself -- `HH:mm <days>` -- is the reminder's own **Ref:** line; Tests/fixtures/rituals/remind.json holds both halves to one table. The WORK grain (D-TA20): the ritual speaks at the grain of the work, not the ticket -- each worker's slot items grouped by milestone title, else by the design card the body names (workThreadRegex, a `> GitHub:` thread; workDesignRegex, a design/ note), else by the title's common stem (workHeadRegex, the head before ' -- ' or ': ', a one-word type tag dropped; two heads share a stem when their first two words or more agree, a trailing small word -- workSmallWordRegex -- not counted), and spoken one phrase per group: text.work<Slot> for the slot's first group, text.workGroup for the rest, {n} a numberWords entry (digits past its end). grains are the three registers of detail the CLI's -Grain and the page's setting choose between. Tests/fixtures/rituals/standup-work.json holds both halves to one table. The PROSE: the work grain is spoken as standup language, one sentence per group -- text.proseSentence joins a lead and a body; the lead is text.prose<Slot> for a slot's (or a queue kind's) first group and text.prose<Slot>Also for the rest; the body is text.proseBare ({item}) for a group of one whose name is its item's clause, else text.prose<Slot>One or text.proseOne for a group of one, else text.prose<Slot>Many or text.proseMany; {item} is text.proseItem (the ref, then the title's head -- workHeadRegex -- as the clause), {refs} the group's refs joined by text.proseRefSeparator. A slot with a text.prose<Slot>Fold template (today's) FOLDS when two or more groups follow its first (D-SA9: a group and a count, never a list): the first group is its sentence as above, and the rest are ONE sentence -- the slot's Also lead, then text.prose<Slot>Fold with {n} the number of groups and {names} their names joined by text.proseNameSeparator, the last by text.proseNameLast, no refs; past proseFoldNames groups it names none, text.prose<Slot>FoldCount. A worker with something to say and no blockers ends on text.proseBlockersNone. Tests/fixtures/rituals/standup-prose.json holds both halves to one table. The DRESS (D-SA11): a model may re-say a worker's prose sentences in the standup register (the agent only, with a model key), and each dressed sentence is held by one guard both halves implement -- dressGuards are its checks, in the order they run, and the first that fails is the reason the prose sentence stands instead: empty (blank, or more than one line), ref-added (a dressRefRegex token -- an issue's #n or a card-id-shaped word -- that is not one of the group's refs), ref-dropped (a ref of the group the sentence does not say), number (a dressNumberRegex number or a numberWords word that is neither the count, a kind count, nor a number in the facts' own words), count-dropped (a group of two or more whose count is not said), kind (a kind noun from the ceremony's kinds said for a kind the group has none of, or after a number that is not that kind's count), name-dropped (the group's name not said, unless the group is one item named by its own clause), name (a capitalised word -- dressNameRegex -- that is not sentence-initial, not dressPronounRegex's I, and not a word of the facts). Tests/fixtures/rituals/standup-dress.json holds both halves to one table. WHAT MOVED: every slot item carries a motion, one of motions -- closed (yesterday's), started or inProgress (today's and the blockers'; started is a card whose **Started:** day, else its **Created:** day, falls in the window; an issue with no card is inProgress) -- and commits, the distinct hashes (regex.commitBullet, group 1, compared by their first seven characters) of its card's `- <hash>` bullets. A detail line says what adds to its slot as text.itemMotion: {motion} is text.motionStarted for a started item, then text.commitOne or commitMany when it has commits, joined by text.countsSeparator; closed (under Yesterday) and in progress (under Today, Blockers) repeat the slot label and are not said, so an item with neither a start nor a commit has no parenthesis. The counts line opens the brief: text.countsTotal, {date} the window's first day in dateFormat and {counts} the non-zero of text.countsClosed, countsStarted, countsInProgress and the commits, joined by countsSeparator, or text.countsNone; a hash is counted once however many cards thread it. Each worker's brief line adds its own started and commits. A window wider than yesterday (Standup -Since, ?since=) says countsClosed for a worker's closes, not briefClosed. THE SUGGESTION (docs/modules/solitaire-agile.md, "The suggestion: one next move, derived"): one derived next move over the joined list, never invented -- exclusions in suggestExclusions's order (notBillable, waiting -- on the queue, the narrower rule that stays first, D-AR7 -- inFlight, theirs -- an issue assigned to someone who is not you, the signed-in gh user; when gh cannot say who you are every assignee is someone else -- dismissed), then severity (the triage ceremony's severities, in order, before none), the nearest milestone (fewest open, then the earlier due date, then title, ordinal; none after every milestone), age (the oldest created day first) and the id, ordinal. Its shape is one of suggestShapes: start (alone, or agents with the item yours, or sized suggestOwnerSeat -- the owner's own seat, never a crew delegation, D-AR10), delegate (agents, a crew size label and a milestone -- well defined), route (agents and nobody has it), place (agents, a crew size and no milestone: text.suggestPlace, and text.suggestCommandPlace for an issue -- Route's milestone write on the tracker -- or text.suggestCommandPlaceCard for a card, Plan's write of its **Sprint:** line). text.suggestStart / suggestDelegate / suggestRoute are the sentences, {why} one of text.suggestWhyLast (its milestone has one open item: it), suggestWhyMilestone and suggestWhyOldest, {kind} its severity else its noun (text.suggestNounCard / suggestNounIssue), {nobody} text.suggestNobody when nobody has it. text.suggestNext is the chair's Next line, {command} the CLI prefix and text.suggestCommandStart or suggestCommandRoute; it replaces briefNextNone only, and only when nothing waits. Tests/fixtures/suggestion/table.json holds both halves to one table. THE CORNER (docs/modules/solitaire-agile.md, "The PM Corner: the line, the chevron, the confetti"): one derived line at the head of the Team Agile page and the last line of the brief, over the same joined list. A milestone REACHED -- an item that names it closed in the standup's window and none that names it is still open -- reads text.cornerReached (shape reached; the latest close first, then the title, ordinal) and is the page's one celebration. Otherwise the nearest milestone among the suggestion's candidates (the suggestion's own order and its nearest-milestone function), its remaining count the open billable items that name it, once per id: one is text.cornerOneLeft ({noun} text.suggestNounCard or suggestNounIssue, by the pick), more is text.cornerManyLeft ({noun} text.cornerNounCards, cornerNounIssues, or cornerNounItems for a mix), {ref} the suggestion's pick inside that milestone. No milestone in reach is text.cornerNothingInReach. cornerShapes names the four. The brief prints text.cornerBriefCommand when the line has a pick ({chevron} text.cornerChevron, {command} the CLI prefix and text.suggestCommandStart), else text.cornerBrief. Tests/fixtures/rituals/corner.json holds both halves to one table.

text.title: Standup -- {date}
text.noWorkers: No worker labels in this Space.
text.adoTracker: Azure DevOps is the human team's board, and its standup is the one the team holds; Team Agile reads a GitHub Space's issues and cards, or a local Space's cards.
text.checkCardArchived: {item} -- the card is archived, but the issue is still open.
text.checkIssueClosed: {item} -- the issue is closed, but the card is not archived.
text.briefInFlightUnknown: In flight is not yet known: every routed issue reads as open.
text.briefNextNone: Next: nothing is waiting on you.
text.suggestDelegate: {ref} is {size}-sized and well defined -- send it to the crew?
text.suggestPlace: {ref} is {size}-sized but has no milestone -- place it?
text.cornerOneLeft: one more {noun} {ref} to get milestone {milestone} - start it now
text.cornerManyLeft: {n} more {noun} to get milestone {milestone} - start {ref} now
text.cornerNothingInReach: no milestone in reach - place a card with Route or on its Sprint line
text.proseLook: Waiting on you to look at

startWork._: Team Agile's hand-off block (StartWork; docs/modules/solitaire-agile.md, "StartWork: the hand-off block"). The CLI builds the block and the web's copy box shows it verbatim, finding the block's title by the head line's shape, so the four heading templates live here (D-AR5): head is the block's first line, then howWeWork, work and prompt open its three sections, each naming the file it came from in {source} so an agent can re-read the original. {kind} is the card's type (Task, Feature, User Story) or Issue; {id} is the card's id or #<n>; {space} is the Space's display name. Which prompt a kind gets is configuration, not contract: config.default.json startWork.prompts. Tests/fixtures/start-work/ holds the block byte for byte. launchEnvFlag is the literal name of the top-level boolean GET /api/env carries for the launch (StartWork <id> -Launch, D-AR12/D-AR13): true where the launch can start a session on this machine; the web's copy box draws its second button, Launch, only when it is true, and an agent that serves no such field reads as off. The agent serves it and the web reads it by this name, so neither half types it.
